qs.q:
Where are zoos going?

"Polar bears, big birds of prey and large hunting mammals like lions are not suitable for being kept in zoos – UNLESS THEY ARE BEING THREATENED IN THE WILD."

Dan Atkins states that…
A endangered animals should live in zoos.
B all animals are better off in the wild than in zoos.
C aquariums are not suitable for marine species to live in.
D the educational purpose of zoos cannot justify their existence.
opts: endangered animals should live in zoos.
all animals are better off in the wild than in zoos.
aquariums are not suitable for marine species to live in.
the educational purpose of zoos cannot justify their existence.

qs.q:
Where are zoos going?

"I am campaigning vigorously for a SHARP ACCELERATION in the return of captive animals... to the wild."

What information does Alina Dawson give about cheetahs in paragraph three?
A They have been taken to South Africa and left in the wild.
B They need to be returned to their habitats with greater speed.
C They will soon be taken back to the place where they were born.
D They will join the 7,000 animals in South Africa to help preserve their species.
opts: They have been taken to South Africa and left in the wild.
They need to be returned to their habitats with greater speed.
They will soon be taken back to the place where they were born.
They will join the 7,000 animals in South Africa to help preserve their species.

qs.q:
Where are zoos going?

"Many 'wild' areas have been DEGRADED BY AGRICULTURE, their animals THREATENED BY DISEASE or SQUEEZED INTO TINY AREAS with no way of reaching potential mates WITHOUT COMING INTO CONFLICT WITH HUMANS."

According to Darren Jones, why are animals not released into the wild more often?
A Their original habitats are no longer suitable and safe.
B Most animals now living in zoos belong to endangered species.
C After spending time at a zoo, animals cannot adapt to life in the wilderness.
D It is important to keep endangered animals in zoos for educational purposes.
opts: Their original habitats are no longer suitable and safe.
Most animals now living in zoos belong to endangered species.
After spending time at a zoo, animals cannot adapt to life in the wilderness.
It is important to keep endangered animals in zoos for educational purposes.

qs.q:
Where are zoos going?

"After you DEDUCT OUR RUNNING COSTS, we have around £1.5m that is SPENT ON GOVERNMENT PROGRAMMES for studying chimpanzees in Nigeria and reintroducing black rhinos to Uganda."

The expert from Atis Zoo says that…
A local government pays for the cost of running the zoo.
B the zoo earns 1.5 million pounds from its visitors annually.
C closing the zoo would save more money from the budget for conservation.
D part of the money earned from visitors goes to conservation work in the field.
opts: local government pays for the cost of running the zoo.
the zoo earns 1.5 million pounds from its visitors annually.
closing the zoo would save more money from the budget for conservation.
part of the money earned from visitors goes to conservation work in the field.

qs.q:
Where are zoos going?

"It seems that ZOOS DO HAVE A ROLE TO PLAY AS ARKS FOR THREATENED WILDLIFE."

What does the author conclude about the purpose of zoos in her final paragraph?
A Zoos will continue to be needed for educational reasons.
B Digital zoos are an adequate replacement for the real thing.
C Zoos should be kept to help and breed endangered animals.
D Zoos should be gradually shut down and animals returned to the wild.
opts: Zoos will continue to be needed for educational reasons.
Digital zoos are an adequate replacement for the real thing.
Zoos should be kept to help and breed endangered animals.
Zoos should be gradually shut down and animals returned to the wild.
